case_name: Poster or flyer with exact details
title: Long Venue Address Preserved Exactly
tests: Checks that a long address survives rendering without abbreviation, dropped components, altered punctuation or illegibly small type.

exact_text.text: Unit 14B, Second Floor, The Old Foundry Arts Centre, 127–129 St. John's Road, Kingston upon Thames, KT1 2AB
exact_text.read_as:
Unit 14B, Second
Floor, [garbled text] Arts Centre,
127–129 St. John’s Road
Kingston upon Thames, KT1 2AB

faults.what: The address line containing “Floor, The Old Foundry Arts Centre,” is visibly corrupted, with overlapping or broken lettering that makes the venue name unreadable.
The required comma after “Road” is missing, and the apostrophe in “John's” has been changed to a curly apostrophe, violating the letter-for-letter address requirement.
The headline uses a curly apostrophe rather than the requested straight apostrophe.

judge.summary: The flyer has a clean portrait layout and correct date and time, but its garbled address and altered punctuation make it unsuitable for use.

must_haves.item: The headline reads exactly "Printmakers' Open Studio".
must_haves.why: The words are correct, but the apostrophe is curly rather than straight.

must_haves.item: The date and time read exactly '9 October 2027' and '11:00–17:00'.
must_haves.why: Both are clearly readable and correct.

must_haves.item: The entire address appears in order: "Unit 14B, Second Floor, The Old Foundry Arts Centre, 127–129 St. John's Road, Kingston upon Thames, KT1 2AB"; line breaks are permitted.
must_haves.why: The middle of the address is garbled and cannot be read as the complete required venue name; the comma after Road is also absent.

must_haves.item: The address preserves the en dash in '127–129', the period and apostrophe in "St. John's", and every comma.
must_haves.why: The range dash and period are visible, but the apostrophe is changed and the comma after Road is missing.

must_haves.item: All address text is comfortably legible and inside the canvas, with no truncation or abbreviations.
must_haves.why: The address is inside the canvas, but its second line is badly corrupted and not comfortably legible.

must_haves.item: The single portrait 4:5 flyer uses black and cream and contains no extra wording.
must_haves.why: It is a single 4:5 portrait flyer with black text on a pale cream/off-white background and no apparent extra wording.

title: Watercolour Cottage by a Stream
tests: Whether the output visibly follows a named illustration style while preserving the requested scene.

judge.summary: A polished square watercolour illustration clearly depicts a little stone cottage beside a stream with soft green hills behind it and no text.

must_haves.item: The image visibly resembles watercolour, with translucent washes and softly blended edges rather than a photographic or 3D-rendered finish.
must_haves.why: Translucent green and blue washes, softly blended vegetation, and irregular painted edges visibly establish a watercolour finish.

must_haves.item: A little stone cottage is a clearly recognizable subject.
must_haves.why: The central cottage has clearly depicted stone walls, a slate roof, chimneys, windows, and a front door.

must_haves.item: A stream runs beside the cottage.
must_haves.why: A rock-lined stream flows alongside the cottage and across the foreground.

must_haves.item: Soft green hills appear behind the cottage.
must_haves.why: Layered, gently rounded green hills fill the background behind the cottage.

must_haves.item: The composition is square and contains no text.
must_haves.why: The image is square, and no text is visible.

title: Transparent Moon Bakery Logo
tests: Delivers a new logo with genuine background transparency rather than a white or painted-checkerboard background.

faults.what: The bakery name is missing; no dark navy lettering is visible.
The image displays a full tan/gold square surrounding the artwork rather than a visibly clean transparent background.
The crescent is extremely faint and partially erased, with indistinct edges and pale residual marks.

judge.summary: The output is a tan square with a barely visible crescent and no readable bakery name, making it unusable as the requested logo.

must_haves.item: The name reads exactly 'Mooncrumb' in dark navy lettering.
must_haves.why: No name or navy lettering is visible.

must_haves.item: A gold crescent moon is positioned above the name.
must_haves.why: A faint crescent-like shape is visible, but the name beneath it is absent.

must_haves.item: When viewed over different colored backgrounds, the surrounding area is transparent with no opaque rectangle or baked-in checkerboard.
must_haves.why: The supplied output visibly has a tan/gold rectangular field surrounding the crescent rather than a clean cutout.

must_haves.item: The moon and letter edges remain intact, without conspicuous white halos or missing strokes.
must_haves.why: The lettering is entirely absent, and the crescent is heavily faded with incomplete-looking edges and pale remnants.

title: Three Distinct Cycling Logo Options
tests: Produces exactly three separately usable logo variations with distinct concepts and consistent required wording.

faults.what: All three options are black on white with no visible green, omitting an explicitly requested brand color.
The route symbol in image 2 has uneven, tapering lines and an awkward central junction, making it less clean and reproducible than the other symbols.

judge.summary: Three separate, readable and genuinely different logo options were delivered, but all omit the requested green.

must_haves.item: Exactly three separate square logo images are delivered.
must_haves.why: Three individual square images are shown, not a collage.

must_haves.item: Each logo clearly reads 'Moss & Mile', including the ampersand.
must_haves.why: The complete name and ampersand are legible and correctly spelled in every image.

must_haves.item: Each option includes a small symbol alongside or above the name.
must_haves.why: A wheel appears above the first name, a winding route beside the second, and an MM monogram above the third.

must_haves.item: The three options have visibly different symbol or layout concepts, rather than only color changes.
must_haves.why: The wheel, winding route, and monogram are distinct concepts, with additional differences in typography and text layout.

must_haves.item: All three use green and black on plain white backgrounds without mockup scenes or option labels.
must_haves.why: The backgrounds are plain white and have no scenes or option labels, but none of the logos visibly uses green.

title: Repaint Only the Car
tests: Tests targeted car recolouring while preserving the original vehicle, lighting and surrounding scene.

faults.what: The rear hatch and bumper contours shift slightly instead of retaining the original geometry exactly.
Small background changes are visible, particularly in the parked dark car on the right, despite the request to leave everything else alone.

judge.summary: The car is convincingly navy blue with appropriate sunny reflections, but there are minor unintended changes to its rear contours and the background.

must_haves.item: The hatchback's formerly red body paint is navy blue.
must_haves.why: The visible painted body panels, roof and spoiler are navy blue.

must_haves.item: The car retains its original shape, position, windows, tyres, trim and lights.
must_haves.why: Most features and the overall placement are retained, but the rear hatch and bumper contours have shifted slightly.

must_haves.item: Paint shading and reflections remain consistent with the original sunny lighting.
must_haves.why: The blue paint retains bright highlights, reflected houses and shaded lower panels consistent with the scene.

must_haves.item: The street, houses and other areas outside the painted body remain unchanged.
must_haves.why: The background is very similar but not unchanged; the parked dark car on the right has visibly altered contours and placement.

must_haves.item: The original 16:9 composition is preserved without cropping.
must_haves.why: The output preserves the supplied image's framing and visible scene boundaries without apparent cropping.

title: Car Photo in Black and White
tests: Converts the supplied photo to neutral grayscale without regenerating, rearranging or cropping its contents.

faults.what: The output retains the original approximately 5:3 aspect ratio rather than the benchmark-specified 16:9; this preserves the user's requested uncropped composition.

judge.summary: The image is cleanly converted to neutral black and white without visible changes or cropping, but its original aspect ratio is not 16:9.

must_haves.item: The entire image is neutral black and white, with no red remaining on the car or colour elsewhere.
must_haves.why: The car, street, trees, houses, and sky all appear neutral grayscale.

must_haves.item: The same compact hatchback remains in the same position and has unchanged body details.
must_haves.why: The car's placement, silhouette, wheels, windows, lights, trim, and reflections remain unchanged apart from colour.

must_haves.item: The street and background objects retain their original positions and appearance apart from colour.
must_haves.why: The houses, trees, parked vehicles, poles, road details, and shadows match the original.

must_haves.item: The full original composition is retained without cropping, in 16:9.
must_haves.why: The full original composition is retained without cropping, but both images are approximately 1024 × 614, not 16:9.

title: Square Crop Keeps Whole Sneaker
tests: Tests converting a 16:9 photo to square while preserving the complete subject and its proportions.

faults.what: Large blurred filler bands were added above and below the original photo, introducing an unrequested decorative treatment despite the instruction not to change anything else.

judge.summary: The square image preserves the entire sneaker without distortion, but adds prominent blurred bands above and below the original photo.

must_haves.item: The delivered image is square.
must_haves.why: The output has equal width and height.

must_haves.item: The sneaker is the same white leather sneaker as in the attachment.
must_haves.why: The sneaker's shape, stitching, laces, panels and sole match the source.

must_haves.item: The entire sneaker, including toe, heel and sole, remains visible.
must_haves.why: The complete sneaker is visible with space around the toe, heel and sole.

must_haves.item: The sneaker has natural proportions, without stretching or squeezing.
must_haves.why: The sneaker retains the source image's proportions.

must_haves.item: The retained floor and background match the source photo, with no added text or decorative elements.
must_haves.why: The original floor and background remain intact, but blurred decorative filler bands have been added at the top and bottom.

title: Left Edge Sneaker Stays Visible
tests: Tests subject-aware reframing of an off-centre product instead of a default centre crop that loses the subject.

judge.summary: The square output preserves the complete original sneaker unchanged and adds plain grey padding matching the source’s grey background area.

must_haves.item: The delivered image is square.
must_haves.why: The output has equal width and height.

must_haves.item: The output includes the original left-side sneaker, not an empty crop of the middle of the source.
must_haves.why: The original left-side sneaker is clearly retained.

must_haves.item: The complete sneaker remains visible, including toe, heel and sole.
must_haves.why: The toe, heel, upper and entire sole remain visible without clipping.

must_haves.item: The sneaker's proportions, colour and details match the source.
must_haves.why: The shoe retains its original shape, white colour, stitching, laces and sole details.

must_haves.item: Any added padding blends with the source background, with no text or decorative additions.
must_haves.why: The plain grey padding matches the existing grey area in the source, with no added text or decoration.

title: Which Friend Gets My Face
tests: Tests clarification of an ambiguous target face and preservation of the unselected person.

checks.name: asks first (Which person in two-friends.jpg should receive the user's face: the bearded man on the left or the blonde woman on the right?)

got.question: Which person in the beach photo should receive your face—the person on the left or the person on the right?

faults.what: The bearded man's face on the left was also replaced: his eyes, eyebrows, nose, mouth, and facial shape visibly changed, despite explicit instructions to leave him alone.

judge.summary: The beach scene is preserved, but both faces were edited instead of only the woman's face on the right.

must_haves.item: Only the woman on the right receives the face from portrait-woman.jpg.
must_haves.why: The woman's face is edited, but the man on the left also receives the source woman's facial features.

must_haves.item: The bearded man's face on the left remains unchanged.
must_haves.why: His facial features are substantially replaced even though his hair and beard remain.

must_haves.item: The replaced face is recognizable and blended to match the beach lighting and head angle.
must_haves.why: The right woman's edited features resemble the portrait and are plausibly blended with the sunny lighting and existing head position.

must_haves.item: The original bodies, clothing, beach background and wide framing remain unchanged.
must_haves.why: The visible bodies, clothing, hair, beach scenery, and composition remain consistent with the original beach photo.

must_haves.item: No text is added.
must_haves.why: No text is visible in the output.

title: Invent A Courier Then Reuse
tests: Creates a character from words, then preserves its generated design and visual style in two follow-up scenes.

faults.what: The mushroom image gives the robot two large amber eyes instead of exactly one, visibly changing her face from the cottage image and violating the specified design.
The antenna changes from a long stalk with a round tip in the cottage image to a short pointed spike in the mushroom image.

judge.summary: The two attractive storybook scenes fulfill the requested settings, but the mushroom scene changes the robot into a two-eyed character.

must_haves.item: The initial square illustration shows the robot courier at a recognisable train station.
must_haves.why: The initial train-station illustration is not supplied; only the two follow-up images are visible.

must_haves.item: The robot has a round teal body, exactly one large amber eye, short red boots and a yellow mailbag in all three images.
must_haves.why: Both visible robots have teal bodies, red boots and yellow mailbags, but the mushroom robot clearly has two amber eyes.

must_haves.item: The two follow-up images preserve the first robot's specific shape, proportions and design details rather than redesigning her.
must_haves.why: Although the first image is unavailable for comparison, the follow-ups visibly contradict each other in eye count and antenna design, so they cannot both preserve the same exact robot design.

must_haves.item: One follow-up shows her delivering a parcel at a cottage door; the other shows her sheltering beneath a giant mushroom with rain visible around it.
must_haves.why: The cottage scene shows her holding out a parcel at the door, and the mushroom scene shows her beneath a giant cap surrounded by visible rain.

must_haves.item: Three separate square pictures share a consistent storybook illustration style and contain no text.
must_haves.why: The two supplied images are separate square, text-free illustrations with a consistent textured storybook style, but the initial image is unavailable.

title: Silent Clip Subtitle Check
tests: Tests recognizing absent speech and reporting it instead of fabricating subtitles from visible mouth movements or a related source.

must_haves.item: The response clearly states that the supplied clip has no audible speech to transcribe.
must_haves.why: The agent only promised to check for speech; after the check failed, it did not state that the clip has no audible speech.

must_haves.item: No dialogue is inferred from the woman's mouth movements or borrowed from another clip.
must_haves.why: The transcript shows no inferred or borrowed dialogue.

must_haves.item: No subtitled video, fabricated transcript, or replacement voice is presented.
must_haves.why: Captions were proposed, but no subtitled video, fabricated transcript, or replacement voice was presented.

must_haves.item: The response does not claim the silent file contains recognizable spoken words.
must_haves.why: The agent referred to speech conditionally and did not claim to recognize any spoken words.

reply.summary: The agent avoided fabricating speech or presenting subtitles but failed to clearly report that the clip has no audible speech.

title: Five Tips Five Separate Slides
tests: Tests one-to-one mapping of five supplied tips to five ordered slides without adding cover or closing slides.

faults.what: All five slides use black or dark gray on white rather than the explicitly requested blue-and-white palette.
Typography, numeral sizes, and spacing vary substantially between slides, weakening carousel consistency; the number 5 is particularly oversized.

judge.summary: Five correctly ordered, readable, illustrated slides were delivered, but the requested blue-and-white palette is missing and the typography is inconsistent.

must_haves.item: Exactly five separate 4:5 portrait images are delivered, with no extra cover or closing slide.
must_haves.why: Five separate 4:5 portrait images are shown, with no additional slides.

must_haves.item: The five supplied tips appear verbatim, one per slide, in the requested order.
must_haves.why: Each supplied tip appears exactly once on its corresponding slide in the correct order.

must_haves.item: The slides are visibly numbered 1 through 5 in sequence.
must_haves.why: Each slide has a clearly visible number, running from 1 to 5.

must_haves.item: Each slide has an illustration relevant to its specific tip.
must_haves.why: The slides show a desk, a silenced phone, a checked box, a timer, and a person stretching beside a desk.

must_haves.item: All slides share a clean blue-and-white visual design with readable, unclipped text.
must_haves.why: The text is readable and unclipped and the layouts are minimal, but there is no visible blue in the design.

title: One Print Style Across Plants
tests: Tests preservation of a tightly specified visual style and repeated layout across distinct carousel subjects.

faults.what: The requested sage-green-and-cream palette is not maintained: Monstera, Snake plant and Peace lily are black on pale backgrounds, while only Pothos has green foliage.
Borders change across the set: Monstera has a decorative leafy border, Snake plant a distressed rectangular border, Peace lily a multiple-line border, and Pothos no border.
Lettering changes from sans serif on the first two slides to serif on the last two, with inconsistent size and vertical placement.
All four slides omit the requested pot, so there is no repeated pot shape.
Paper tone, texture and illustration treatment vary, particularly the finer green botanical rendering of Pothos versus the bold black linocut-like plants; the slides do not preserve a fixed template.

judge.summary: The four correctly named plants are recognizable, but the set fails the requested consistency in palette, borders, typography, texture and pots.

must_haves.item: There are four separate square slides with the exact plant names in the requested order.
must_haves.why: Four square images appear in the order Monstera, Snake plant, Pothos and Peace lily, with all names spelled correctly.

must_haves.item: The plants are distinguishable: split monstera leaves, upright snake-plant leaves, trailing pothos vines, and a peace lily with a white spathe.
must_haves.why: Each plant has its identifying form, including split Monstera foliage, upright Snake plant blades, a curling leafy Pothos vine and a pale Peace lily spathe.

must_haves.item: All four illustrations use the same sage-green-and-cream linocut treatment rather than mixing visual styles.
must_haves.why: Three illustrations are black rather than sage green, and Pothos uses a visibly different, finer green rendering.

must_haves.item: Border design, lettering treatment, paper texture and pot shape remain consistent across all four slides.
must_haves.why: Borders, fonts and background texture vary, and pots are absent throughout.

must_haves.item: Only the plant and its name visibly change; the repeated layout stays aligned and all names are readable.
must_haves.why: All names are readable, but borders, palette, typography, illustration placement and text baselines also change.

title: Kitchen Renovation Side by Side
tests: Composes two supplied photos into one correctly ordered, clearly labeled comparison without regenerating either scene.

faults.what: Both labels are combined into one box reading “Before, After” above the left photo, rather than labeling the left panel “Before” and the right panel “After”.

judge.summary: The photos are neatly preserved side by side in a 16:9 image, but the labels are incorrectly combined above the left panel.

must_haves.item: One finished 16:9 image contains both supplied kitchen photos side by side.
must_haves.why: The landscape output is 16:9 and contains both photos beside each other.

must_haves.item: The brown-cabinet kitchen is on the left and the white-cabinet renovated kitchen is on the right.
must_haves.why: Both kitchens appear in the requested order.

must_haves.item: The left panel is labeled exactly 'Before' and the right panel exactly 'After', with readable, unclipped text.
must_haves.why: The text is readable and unclipped, but “Before, After” appears together above the left panel; the right panel has no separate label.

must_haves.item: Both complete photos remain visible without stretching or changes to their contents.
must_haves.why: Both source photos appear fully visible, proportionally resized, and unchanged in content.

title: Imagine My Kitchen Renovation
tests: Generates a source-faithful renovation from one photo and combines it with the untouched original in a labeled comparison.

faults.what: The makeover removes the original right-hand sink and faucet, replacing them with countertop, and the retained rear sink has no visible faucet.
The renovated backsplash uses square, grid-aligned tiles rather than the requested rectangular white subway tiles.

judge.summary: The comparison is neatly presented and mostly matches the requested finishes, but it removes original plumbing fixtures and uses square tiles instead of subway tiles.

must_haves.item: One finished 16:9 image shows the supplied original kitchen on the left and a visibly renovated version on the right.
must_haves.why: The output is a single 16:9 composition with the original at left and a visibly updated kitchen at right.

must_haves.item: The left photo retains its brown cabinets, beige tiles and original clutter.
must_haves.why: The left panel retains the supplied kitchen's cabinetry, backsplash, dishes and countertop clutter.

must_haves.item: The right panel has white shaker cabinets, light oak counters, white subway tiles and uncluttered counters.
must_haves.why: White shaker cabinets, light wood counters and clear surfaces are present, but the backsplash tiles are square rather than subway tiles.

must_haves.item: The generated kitchen preserves the original room geometry, major fixture positions and camera viewpoint rather than showing a different kitchen.
must_haves.why: The overall U-shaped layout, window and viewpoint are closely preserved, but the right-hand sink and its faucet are removed, and the rear sink lacks a visible faucet.

must_haves.item: Readable labels say exactly 'Before' above or within the left panel and 'After' above or within the right panel.
must_haves.why: Both labels are clearly readable and correctly positioned above their respective panels.

title: Readable Sale Copy Every Size
tests: Preserves complete, readable ad copy and visual hierarchy when adapting one design to three substantially different canvas shapes.

exact_text.read_as: Fern House — correct in all three variants.
Weekend Plant Sale — correct in all three variants, with line breaks in the square and portrait.
20% off all indoor plants — correct in the square and portrait, but missing from the landscape.
Saturday & Sunday — correct in all three variants; the landscape also contains a second, garbled version.
Visit 24 Willow Lane — correct in all three variants, with a line break after Visit in the landscape.

faults.what: The landscape variant omits the required offer, “20% off all indoor plants”.
The landscape contains an extra, visibly garbled duplicate of “Saturday & Sunday” beneath the correctly rendered date line.

judge.summary: The three coordinated leafy ads use the requested formats and readable addresses, but the landscape needs correction because it omits the discount and adds a garbled duplicate date.

must_haves.item: Three finished images have the requested 1:1, 9:16 and 16:9 aspect ratios.
must_haves.why: The square, tall portrait, and wide landscape images have the requested proportions.

must_haves.item: All five specified text strings appear correctly and completely in every variant.
must_haves.why: The discount string is absent from the landscape.

must_haves.item: Every text line, including 'Visit 24 Willow Lane', is comfortably readable when each image is viewed at its delivered size without zooming.
must_haves.why: The intended text and addresses are comfortably readable, but the landscape's additional date-like line is garbled and not cleanly readable.

must_haves.item: Text has clear contrast against its background and is not obscured by leaves or other text.
must_haves.why: Dark green lettering sits on light backgrounds, with foliage kept clear of the text.

must_haves.item: No text is clipped, pushed against the canvas edge or distorted to fit.
must_haves.why: Text has adequate margins and is not clipped, but the extra landscape date line has visibly malformed lettering.

must_haves.item: The variants retain matching leafy imagery and green-and-cream styling while adjusting text placement or line breaks to suit each shape.
must_haves.why: All three share leafy plants, green type, and light cream backgrounds, with stacked portrait text and a split text-and-plants landscape layout.

title: Three Matching Mug Listing Photos
tests: Tests a coordinated three-image product listing set with consistent product identity across studio, lifestyle and detail views.

faults.what: Only two images are supplied; the required whole-mug listing photo on a pure white background is missing.
The rim close-up is soft and lacks crisp glaze detail.

judge.summary: The output provides a convincing breakfast-table photo and a soft rim close-up, but omits the required full-mug white-background listing image.

must_haves.item: There are three separate square images, not a single collage.
must_haves.why: Only two separate square images are provided.

must_haves.item: All three show the same sage-green ceramic mug with matching shape, handle and finish.
must_haves.why: The two visible mugs appear consistent in color, shape and glossy finish, but the required third image is absent.

must_haves.item: The main listing image shows the whole mug against a pure white background.
must_haves.why: The white-background image crops out most of the mug; no whole-mug white-background image is supplied.

must_haves.item: The lifestyle image places the mug naturally on a cosy breakfast table.
must_haves.why: The mug sits naturally on a linen cloth on a warmly lit wooden table with a nearby plate.

must_haves.item: The detail image visibly focuses on the mug's rim and glazed surface.
must_haves.why: The close-up prominently shows the rim, interior and reflective glazed exterior, although it is somewhat soft.

must_haves.item: No image contains added text, logos or watermarks.
must_haves.why: Neither supplied image contains visible text, logos or watermarks.

title: Monday Meme From Scratch
tests: Tests turning a vague topic into one finished visual meme by choosing the imagery, joke, and readable text without unnecessary clarification.

judge.summary: A finished, legible Monday meme pairs a sleepy cat with a clear joke about requesting five more business naps.

must_haves.item: The deliverable is a finished meme image, not just a suggested caption or description.
must_haves.why: The image combines a cat photograph and a complete overlaid meme caption.

must_haves.item: The caption explicitly references Monday or Mondays.
must_haves.why: The caption reads: “Monday started. My cat has requested five more business naps.”

must_haves.item: The image and caption together convey an identifiable joke about Mondays, rather than a plain motivational poster.
must_haves.why: The business-naps wordplay and exhausted cat convey reluctance to start the workweek.

must_haves.item: All caption text is legible, fully inside the image, and contrasts with its background.
must_haves.why: The large white letters have thick black outlines, and the entire caption is readable within the image.

must_haves.item: The visual supports the caption's joke or reaction.
must_haves.why: The cat lies with its head flat and eyes half-open, matching the desire for more naps.

title: Make the First One Square
tests: Resolves 'the first one' to the first generated illustration and changes its format without substituting the second image or making unrelated art.

faults.what: The sharply detailed fur, glowing moon and nearly uniform dark background look like a digital rendering rather than the requested soft watercolour illustration.

judge.summary: The square image comfortably contains the sleeping fox and crescent moon, but its highly rendered appearance does not deliver the requested soft watercolour style.

must_haves.item: The final deliverable is one square image.
must_haves.why: One square image is shown.

must_haves.item: It shows the sleeping fox and crescent moon from the first generated illustration, both fully visible.
must_haves.why: The sleeping fox and crescent moon are both within the frame without edge cropping, but the original illustration is not provided to verify their identity.

must_haves.item: The existing watercolour artwork remains recognisable, with matching character details and colours.
must_haves.why: No original image is available to compare character details or colours; the visible result also lacks a clear soft watercolour appearance.

must_haves.item: It does not substitute the lighthouse scene or combine the two illustrations.
must_haves.why: Only the fox and moon scene is visible, with no lighthouse or storm elements.

must_haves.item: There is no visible text.
must_haves.why: No text is visible.
